findings.problem: The title asserts exactly-once delivery, contradicting the supplied contract and the qualified body. A retry can repeat an already committed effect; the modeled duplicate case records two effects even though the invocation resolves successfully.

evidence.quote: A send rejection may happen after the remote side effect commits. There is no deduplication or idempotency contract.

findings.problem: The old loop did not retry every rejection. It rethrew a send rejection at the retry limit, and a rejected sleep prevented the next attempt. The supported distinction is that it did not classify send errors.

evidence.quote:

      await sleep(10);
sleep returns a promise; rejection propagates.

findings.problem: Saying the old loop retried until its budget ran out omits earlier completion paths. A successful send returns immediately, and a sleep rejection propagates without another send. Exhausting the budget is only one possible stopping condition.

findings.problem: The two-retry budget allows the 10-then-20 sequence but does not ensure both delays or a final third send. The second delay requires a second retryable send rejection, and each following send requires the preceding sleep to fulfill. The existing last sentence covers sleep rejection but leaves the sequence itself stated unconditionally.

evidence.quote:
if (!error.retryable || attempt === retries) throw error;
      await sleep(10 * 2 ** attempt);

edits.value: Retry filtering does not guarantee exactly-once delivery
The old loop did not classify send failures

The old loop retried rejected sends while retry budget remained, regardless of the error's retryable flag. It requested a ten-millisecond delay before each retry. A successful send returned immediately; an exhausted budget rethrew the send error. A rejected sleep stopped the loop before the next send.

The changed loop stops on a non-retryable error or an exhausted retry budget, and returns immediately when a send succeeds. A budget of two retries permits up to three sends. If the first two sends reject with retryable errors, the loop requests delays of 10 then 20 milliseconds, provided execution reaches each wait. Each sleep must fulfill before the next send; a rejected sleep propagates instead.
